title: Week 18 Mastery Quiz · Semester Examination and Capstone Proposal Defense

questions.question: A proposed thesis question asks 'Why is one regime bad?' What revision makes the project researchable?
options: Keep the value judgment as the only variable
Ask interviewees to confirm the premise
Specify institutions, measurable outcomes, period, cases, and rival explanations
Replace evidence collection with an opinion poll
questions.explanation: Specify institutions, measurable outcomes, period, cases, and rival explanations

questions.question: A senior bibliography contains official texts and commentary but no dates or edition details. What is missing?
options: Only a longer title
An anonymous source
A higher word count
Traceable provenance, edition or date, and citation details
questions.explanation: Traceable provenance, edition or date, and citation details

questions.question: A capstone plan involves identifiable participant interviews. What must be addressed before collection?
options: Consent, minimization of identifying information, safeguarding and appropriate review
Publication of all raw identities
Automatic claims of anonymity without controls
Assuming a classroom exercise eliminates ethical obligations
questions.explanation: Consent, minimization of identifying information, safeguarding and appropriate review

questions.question: A proposal promises causal proof from a single cross-sectional correlation. How should the claim change?
options: The planned correlation proves causation
Frame association cautiously and specify stronger evidence needed for causal inference
Remove all variables
Use the correlation as a final thesis defense
questions.explanation: Frame association cautiously and specify stronger evidence needed for causal inference

questions.question: A mock oral defense asks why a case was selected. Which answer is methodologically strongest?
options: Because the case is well known
Because it agrees with the conclusion
Selection follows stated comparison criteria and allows alternative explanations to be tested
Because the source is easiest to find
questions.explanation: Selection follows stated comparison criteria and allows alternative explanations to be tested

questions.question: A class votes 79–41 on an imagined important UN General Assembly question with all 120 members present and voting. Using Charter Article 18, what follows?
options: 79 is more than half, so it meets every threshold
The vote automatically becomes unanimous
A simple majority and two-thirds are identical
79 falls below the required 80 votes for a two-thirds threshold
questions.explanation: 79 falls below the required 80 votes for a two-thirds threshold

questions.question: A proposal contains four overlapping research questions but time for only one evidence trail. What revision is appropriate?
options: Prioritize a feasible question and define evidence needed within the course timeline
Remove the methods section entirely
Keep all four without boundaries
Treat breadth as proof of scholarly depth
questions.explanation: Prioritize a feasible question and define evidence needed within the course timeline

questions.question: A senior reports an opposing primary source that contradicts the thesis. What demonstrates readiness for defense?
options: Exclude the contrary text
Evaluate its authenticity, relevance, and effect on the argument
Use it as proof the topic is unanswerable
Change the source date to match the thesis
questions.explanation: Evaluate its authenticity, relevance, and effect on the argument

questions.question: The UDHR Article 10 describes rights in a judicial hearing. Which research approach avoids overclaiming?
options: Treat the Declaration as proof that every court complies
Use only commentary about courts
Distinguish the standard expressed from measured access, practice, and remedy in a selected country
Assume all national procedures are legally identical
questions.explanation: Distinguish the standard expressed from measured access, practice, and remedy in a selected country

questions.question: A proposed capstone includes country-level comparisons with no variable definitions. What is the strongest repair?
options: Add more adjectives to the title
Remove comparative cases
Select a desired result first
Operationalize concepts, identify comparable indicators, and disclose limitations
questions.explanation: Operationalize concepts, identify comparable indicators, and disclose limitations

shortResponse: Can the student integrate comparative concepts, institutional evidence, country knowledge, and a defensible research plan?
rubric: 10 points: precise claim (2), accurate concepts (2), two specific pieces of evidence (2), reasoning (2), counterargument or limitation (1), revision condition (1).
